done.why: I had seen most rooms and solved several puzzles. The dragon, the locked lizard door and the crack were still unsolved, and the lamp was dimming, so I stopped.

about: A remixed Zork II. You explore the caverns south of a ravine while a meddling Wizard casts spells on you. The treasures sit behind puzzles: a riddle door, a vault, a dragon, an Alice-style tea room and a baseball-diamond maze.

ending.what: No ending reached. I got the pearls, then died to the poison flask, which sent the necklace to the Wizard's cabinet. I never got past the dragon or the locked lizard door.

moments.note: The Wizard appears and drops hints, then fumbles me and I drop the lamp.
The grue in lit light is revealed as an illusion of the Wizard's.
The baseball-diamond maze: the window glows brighter with each correct step.
Answered 'well' to the riddle and the stone door opened onto the pearls.
The water-filled bucket rides me up the well.
Opening the skull-and-crossbones flask killed me. I respawned in the red mist spheres, and the pearls went to the Wizard's cabinet.
The carousel room's random exits made every trip back to the riddle room a long guessing loop.
Taking the blue cake out of the tea room crumbled it, so I could not return to normal size that way.
Could not find a way past the dragon even though the Wizard had made me fireproof.

wished: A clearer way to leave the carousel on purpose.
Some hint about the dragon and the lamp reflection.
Somewhere to find the small key for the lizard door.
To learn what finishing the diamond maze actually did.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: The Wizard's look gives a real goal and a nudge in the same breath.

lines.line: A real one would have had you by now. It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room
lines.why: A funny, self-aware explanation of the illusion.

lines.line: As you pass out, you realize that the vapors from the flask's contents are fatal.
lines.why: A sudden death that cost me my treasure.

fun.why: Many distinct puzzles and a mischievous Wizard kept things lively. The carousel's random exits and a few dead ends dragged.

engagement.why: There was always another room or object to try. Some leads, like the diamond maze payoff and the dragon, stayed open.

difficulty.why: Some puzzles were well signposted, like the riddle and the bucket. The dragon and the maze payoff were opaque, and the random carousel was tedious.

interestingness.why: Rooms varied a lot: bank, Alice tea room, baseball maze, mist spheres. Descriptions carried useful hints.

prose.why: Witty and informative object descriptions that hint at solutions. Some of the Wizard's lines were very good.
